common_name: Charles Lamont Viburnum (Pink Winter-Flowering Bodnant Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, choosing a spot sheltered from harsh winter wind so buds are not damaged before they open.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, ideally in a spot sheltered from cutting winter wind. 'Charles Lamont' is a vigorous, upright selection of the winter-flowering Bodnant viburnum hybrid, valued for producing denser, showier clusters of rose-pink, tubular flowers than the older 'Dawn' cultivar, opening intermittently on bare branches from late autumn through late winter whenever a mild spell arrives. The sweetly fragrant blooms carry well on calm days, making it worth siting near a walkway or window. Coarse, dull-green leaves emerge with a bronze cast in spring and give modest reddish fall color before dropping to reveal the winter flower display. Renewal-prune a few of the oldest stems to the ground after flowering every few years to keep the multi-stemmed shrub from thinning out at the base.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, in a location where late-season fragrance and pale winter flowers can be enjoyed up close.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. 'Deben' is a Bodnant viburnum selection whose flower buds open blush pink but quickly fade to near white, giving the winter display a softer, two-tone look than the deeper pink of 'Dawn' or 'Charles Lamont', though the same sweet fragrance carries on mild days from late fall into late winter. Frost can tinge the open flowers pink again before they finally fall, adding extra interest to the bare, upright branches. Dull, toothed leaves emerge bronzy in spring and turn dull red-purple in fall on this multi-stemmed, vigorous shrub. Renewal-prune the oldest canes to the base every few years right after flowering to maintain vigorous new wood, since flowers form on the previous year's growth.

common_name: Straight and Narrow Arrowwood Viburnum (Columnar Native Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade; the narrow, upright habit makes it well suited to tight side yards, foundation rows, or informal screens where width is limited.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained to consistently moist soil in full sun to partial shade; this native arrowwood selection tolerates clay and periodic wet spells once established. 'Straight and Narrow' is prized for a tight, columnar habit that stays only 2 to 3 feet wide even as it reaches 6 to 8 feet tall, making it useful as a narrow hedge or vertical accent where a standard arrowwood viburnum's broad spread would not fit. Flat clusters of creamy white flowers appear in late spring, followed by blue-black fruit that draws birds in fall, and the glossy dark green leaves turn shades of orange and red before dropping. Because it flowers and fruits on multiple stems rather than a single leader, little corrective pruning is needed beyond removing the occasional wayward shoot to preserve the columnar outline.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; site it where the heavy, long-lasting coral-pink fruit clusters can be viewed from a distance in fall.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; heaviest fruiting occurs in full sun. Released by the U.S. National Arboretum as a sibling selection to 'Michael Dodge' and 'Catskill', 'Erie' is grown chiefly for its unusually persistent coral-pink to salmon fruit, which ripens in late summer and can remain showy on the arching branches well into winter since birds tend to leave it alone longer than the red-fruited types. Flat clusters of creamy white flowers open in late spring ahead of the fruit display, and the coarse, felted leaves take on bronze-red fall color. The rounded, dense shrub stays more compact than the species overall, fitting mixed borders and foundation plantings where a smaller linden viburnum is wanted. Prune only lightly right after flowering, since flower buds and fruit form on the previous season's wood.

common_name: Park Farm Hybrid Viburnum (Fragrant Burkwood Selection)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Park Farm Hybrid blooms on old wood, so prune only right after flowering.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. 'Park Farm Hybrid' is an early-raised Burkwood viburnum selection valued for a lower, broader, more spreading habit than the typical upright species form, along with especially large, rounded clusters of pink buds that open white and carry the same intense, spicy-sweet fragrance in mid to late spring. Glossy, dark green leaves are semi-evergreen in milder winters and turn maroon-red where the plant sheds fully in fall, and small red fruit that ripens to black follows the flowers. Its wider, more informal outline suits it to massing or a mixed shrub border rather than the tighter foundation spots better suited to upright forms. Prune lightly immediately after bloom only if needed, since later cuts remove the next year's flower buds.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Diana blooms on old wood, so avoid pruning until right after flowers fade.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun. 'Diana' stands apart from other Korean spice viburnum cultivars for foliage that emerges deep maroon-purple in spring before settling to a bronzed dark green through summer, adding season-long color beyond the flowers. Dense clusters of dark pink buds open to soft pink-tinged white blooms in early to mid spring, carrying the same intensely spicy-sweet fragrance the species is known for. Fall color deepens to wine-red and purple, echoing the spring foliage tones. Like other Korean spice viburnums it needs reliable winter chill to flower well and can be lackluster in zone 8 and warmer. Site it where the colored new growth and fragrance are both easily seen, and prune only lightly right after bloom.
